web_evidence.title: Jean M. Auel Writing Styles in The Valley of Horses
web_evidence.note: The study guide explicitly identifies third-person omniscient narration and explains that chapters alternate focal attention between Ayla and Jondalar while remaining in the same grammatical person.

web_evidence.title: The Valley of Horses Quotes
web_evidence.note: Quoted passages attributed to Chapters 1, 2, and 4 narrate Ayla and Jondalar externally in third person, corroborating the whole-book POV description across both storylines.

search_log: Searched "The Valley of Horses" "Jean M. Auel" official excerpt publisher, first chapter, and Google Books preview; Penguin Random House supplied only synopsis copy, while Google Books exposed only a limited-preview record.

Searched "The Valley of Horses" point of view, third person, omniscient, and narrator; opened the BookRags style analysis, which explicitly describes the novel's whole-book third-person omniscient structure.
Searched exact opening text and chapter excerpts; opened the BookRags quotation page containing third-person passages from Chapters 1, 2, and 4.

Opened the Open Library record for the 1982 Crown first edition; it exposed only the first sentence and a preview-only notice. Its linked Library of Congress sample returned HTTP 403, so neither was used as diagnostic prose evidence.

Searched for epistolary, diary, frame narrative, first-person narration, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view. Results described parallel or alternating Ayla/Jondalar storylines but produced no evidence of sustained first- or second-person base sections.
Opened publisher, Kirkus, and other structural-summary results; their synopsis grammar was treated as nondiagnostic, and an unauthorized online transcription was not used as evidence.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and third person. Multiple Goodreads passages independently show external access to Ayla's and Jondalar's actions, memories, sensations, and private thoughts. The many I, we, and you forms occur in dialogue or gnomic material, not base narration. Web research explicitly describes third-person omniscient narration with alternating Ayla- and Jondalar-focused chapters; alternating focal characters therefore do not warrant ALTERNATING. No credible contrary person evidence was found. Confidence is medium because the explicit whole-book web description and corroborating chapter quotations are Tier C, and the authorized library sample could not be accessed.
